wins.text: Noninterest income increased 19% YoY with growth across most categories, more than offsetting the expected NII decline; sixth consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth
EPS of $1.33 per diluted share grew from both Q1 and a year ago, with net income of $4.9 billion
Repurchased $6.1 billion of common stock in Q2 and over $12 billion in H1 2024; announced 14% dividend increase to $0.40/share in Q3
Markets revenue grew 16% YoY driven by strong performance in equities, structured products and credit; trading assets up ~17% on average
CET1 ratio of 11% remains well above current 8.9% regulatory minimum plus buffers and above the new 9.8% minimum effective Q4 2024

risks.text: Full-year 2024 NII now guided to down ~8%-9% vs. 2023, remaining in the upper half of original range but reflecting weaker-than-expected loan balances and a surprise ~$350M headwind from WIM sweep deposit repricing in June

Full-year 2024 noninterest expense guidance raised to ~$54B from original ~$52.6B, driven by higher operating losses/customer remediation accruals (~$500M above run rate YTD), $336M FDIC special assessment, and higher WIM revenue-related comp

Commercial real estate office losses remain elevated and lumpy; nonperforming assets rose 5% QoQ driven by higher CRE office nonaccruals; office commitment down 13% and loan balances down 9% YoY but uncertainty persists
Average loans declined from both Q1 and a year ago across most categories; tepid commercial loan demand expected to persist with balances declining slightly from Q2 levels into H2 2024

Asset cap continues to constrain trading and markets business growth; Basel III finalization uncertainty causing management to slow buyback pace and maintain conservative capital posture near 11% CET1

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2024 NII now expected to be down ~8%-9% vs. 2023 (upper half of original -7% to -9% range), reflecting weaker loan balances and ~$350M WIM sweep repricing headwind not in original guide

Full-year 2024 noninterest expense raised to ~$54B from original ~$52.6B guidance, driven by higher operating losses/remediation (~$500M above run rate YTD), $336M FDIC special assessment, and higher WIM revenue-related comp
Q3 common stock dividend expected to increase 14% to $0.40/share, subject to Board approval
WIM advisory asset-based fees expected to increase in Q3 based on higher market valuations as of July 1 vs. April 1; credit card charge-off rate expected to decline in Q3

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Rationale and competitive context for the WIM sweep deposit repricing decision in June
Sustainability and market share trajectory of trading/markets revenue going forward
Granular breakdown of operating loss and remediation expense overages vs. original guidance
